Is inline HTML possible for the sidebar?

No, HTML is not accepted anywhere on this site. This is pretty common for most sites now to prevent malicious content from being injected, unlike 10 years ago where you could input HTML willy nilly and force MySpace to shut down after gaining 1 million friends.

One thing you need to know about Markdown is that it is a specification for a markup language, but individual implementations vary. Mr Gruber (of daringfireball.net) is of course the original author, though Markdown has evolved entirely beyond his control now. There are dozens of popular Markdown implementations in different programming languages; Voat uses MarkdownDeep for C#. Big sites like Github, Stack Exchange, and reddit all use their own “flavour” of Markdown with slightly different rules.

Moving on, the key to styling your sidebar is to use whatever elements are available in Markdown. If you look at the sidebar on this very sub, the purple boxes are each formed by a level-5 header and a blockquote, which would look something like this in Markdown:

##### Welcome to CustomizingVoat

> Hey, there! This sub's dedicated to…

and will result in HTML output like this:

<h5>Welcome to CustomizingVoat</h5>
<blockquote>Hey, there! This sub's dedicated to…</blockquote>

You will need to target your CSS carefully. You don’t want every blockquote, including those in posts and comments, to turn into a purple box, so your selector should be something like .side .titlebox blockquote. This sub uses .side .md h5 + blockquote to cleverly target only blockquotes that immediately follow a h5 element.

how did they know to use ".leavemoderator" (very top) or ".tabmenu" (page down) or ".side" to start out a section?

By inspecting the output of the page. I suggest Chrome or Firefox as they have the best developer tools. Right-clicking the element you want to examine and choosing Inspect Element. You then work up the hierarchy from your target element to find unique parents that you can refer to by class or ID.

For example, if you inspect one of the purple boxes and find the blockquote, you'll see that its parent (and its parent’s parent etc) are, in order:

  • a <div> of class “md”
  • a <div> of class “usertext-body”
  • a <form> of id “form-xxxxx”
  • a <div> of class “titlebox”
  • a <div> of class “spacer”
  • a <div> of class “side”
  • and so on and so forth.

There’s no hard and fast rule for which elements you should use to narrow down your selection. We can see that div.spacer is not particularly unique, so that’s not a good way to target our sidebar. If you poke around a bit you’ll find that div.titlebox is unique, so that’s a good target. Here’s a terrible illustration of what to look out for in the inspector.
